A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LiveCodeBench and retain the same four evaluation scenarios and Appendices A-E. The text, figures, tables, and code examples are readable and can be matched across the expanded and relocated material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original model evaluations, Pass@1 results, and contamination analyses. Appendix E supplies observed code-execution failures.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds results for newer models, additional contamination cases, and revised benchmark statistics.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.2 extend benchmark construction by collecting platform autograder failure cases for recent LeetCode problems, supplementing the public tests and generator-produced tests described in v1. The four task procedures, prompting schemes, and self-repair mechanism remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four Python coding scenarios using LeetCode, AtCoder, and CodeForces, with HumanEval+ comparisons. The additional problems extend the existing contest stream through May 2024; they change sample counts and evaluation windows within retained coverage, without adding a platform, domain, language, or task.

E2.justification: Tables 3-6 substantially expand the evaluated comparison set, including Llama 3, CodeGemma, CodeQwen, GPT-4-O, Gemini 1.5, Codestral, and OpenCodeInterpreter variants, with participation varying by scenario. WizardCoder-33B and WizardCoder-34B disappear from Tables 3-5, while WizardCoder-34B gains a direct code-execution entry in Table 6.

E3.justification: The generation/repair collection extends from February to May 2024, increasing the full pool from 400 to 511 and the post-September pool from 238 to 349. Table 1 reports average tests per problem falling from 59.2 to 17.0. New contamination comparisons introduce additional cutoff windows. Default decoding and prompts remain unchanged; these reported changes do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing temporal contamination analysis gains GPT-4-O cases in Figures 1, 10, and 11, plus Codestral's pre-/post-February comparison in Section 5.1. These extend an established analysis. The CoT comparisons and Appendix E's five qualitative failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces explicit n=1 annotations, including Gemini-Pro-1.5-April in Tables 4-6, alongside the retained general statement of ten candidates per problem. Section 7 changes the bootstrap sample/pool sizes from 238/400 to 349/511 while retaining the 1-1.5% variability estimate. No new confidence intervals or significance tests are provided.

E6.justification: Tables 3-6 add extensive results and revise retained scores. For example, the new GPT-4-O entry reports 41.9 for generation, 49.1 for repair, 68.9 for test-output prediction, and 91.0 for CoT execution; GPT-4-Turbo-1106's reported CoT execution score changes from 84.7 to 83.6. Section 5.2 changes the HumanEval+ correlation from 0.77 to 0.72. Generation scores involve revised evaluation conditions and do not establish same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The task and correctness definitions remain unchanged, and neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs. v2's explicit statement that programs must pass all tests restates the existing correctness criterion.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a live benchmark covering four coding capabilities. The introduction broadens the contamination finding from DeepSeek to GPT-4-O and Codestral, and revises the leading open-model claims to include Llama 3 and Mixtral.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly states that DeepSeek pretraining contamination affects its instruction-tuned descendants. Section 5.2 removes speculation about training schedules and the explanation that instruction tuning primarily elicits existing capabilities. The introduction adds a speed rationale for fewer tests; the substantive language, domain, and prompt-sensitivity limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 expands model identifiers, links, and cutoff metadata, including details for previously unlisted base models. Reported DeepSeek cutoffs change from July 30 to August 30, 2023, and Claude-3 Opus/Sonnet cutoffs from July 30 to April 30, 2023. Detailed prompts, generator instructions, filtering criteria, and release information otherwise remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds CodeScope (Yan et al., 2023), updates the model landscape to include Llama 3, and expands the stated differentiation from prior benchmarks to emphasize balanced difficulty, test/problem quality, and agentic coding systems. Most related-work discussion and references are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, curation description, and results receive targeted revisions. 'Instruction tuning' becomes 'post training' in one discussion, and several model names are standardized. The section order and appendix organization remain intact, with substantial text unchanged.

P2.justification: Retained plots gain model series, revised legends, axes, and cutoff shading while preserving their basic chart forms. Table 2 extends across two pages, Tables 5 and 6 move onto separate pages, and result-table captions move below the tables. Figure 5 becomes more compact, and v2's Table 3 overlaps its page number.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful model comparisons, recent problems, and contamination cases. However, the reduction from 59.2 to 17.0 tests per problem is not accompanied by an analysis establishing its effect on correctness detection, despite the added platform failure cases. Table 6 also introduces unexplained -1.00 Pass@1 entries. The empirical breadth improves, but the unresolved evaluation and reporting issues prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality.
